CYTOGENETICS AND MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
Sex: Female
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]

SPECIMEN INFORMATION
Specimen Type: Solid tissue
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Referring Clinician: Dr. [redacted name]
Clinical Details: Infant patient referred for genetic testing

TESTS PERFORMED
1. Multiplex Ligation-dependent Probe Amplification (MLPA) - Subtelomere screening
2. Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) - Aneuploidy screening

TEST METHODOLOGY

MLPA ANALYSIS
DNA was extracted from solid tissue specimen using standard protocols. MLPA analysis was performed using the SALSA MLPA P036 and P070 Human Telomere probe mixes (MRC-Holland), which contain probes for all chromosome subtelomere regions. The procedure included:
- DNA denaturation and hybridization with MLPA probes
- Ligation of hybridized probes
- PCR amplification using fluorescent primers
- Fragment analysis on ABI 3730 Genetic Analyzer
- Data analysis using Coffalyser.Net software

QF-PCR ANALYSIS
QF-PCR was performed on uncultured tissue DNA using polymorphic short tandem repeat (STR) markers:
- Chromosome 13: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742
- Chromosome 18: D18S535, D18S391, D18S858
- Chromosome 21: D21S1435, D21S1411, D21S1446
- X chromosome: AMELX, DXS6803, DXS6809
- Y chromosome: AMELY, SRY

Amplification was performed using fluorescent primers, and products were analyzed on ABI 3730 Genetic Analyzer with GeneMapper software.

RESULTS

MLPA SUBTELOMERE ANALYSIS
Result: NORMAL
No subtelomeric deletions or duplications detected

All subtelomere regions showed normal copy number with probe ratios between 0.85-1.15 (normal range: 0.70-1.30). Quality control parameters met acceptable criteria with standard deviation <0.10.

QF-PCR ANEUPLOIDY SCREENING
Chromosome 13: Normal diallelic pattern - TWO COPIES
Chromosome 18: Normal diallelic pattern - TWO COPIES  
Chromosome 21: Normal diallelic pattern - TWO COPIES
Sex chromosomes: XX pattern detected - FEMALE

All informative markers showed expected 1:1 peak ratios for autosomes. No evidence of triploidy detected.

INTERPRETATION
The combined MLPA and QF-PCR analyses show:
1. No subtelomeric imbalances detected in any chromosome
2. Normal copy number for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21
3. Female sex chromosome complement (XX)
4. No evidence of triploidy

These results exclude subtelomere imbalance and aneuploidy of the tested chromosomes. The findings confirm a normal chromosome complement for all tested regions.

LIMITATIONS
- This analysis cannot detect balanced chromosomal rearrangements
- Low-level mosaicism (<20%) may not be detected
- Small imbalances below the resolution of MLPA probes (~100-200kb) will not be detected
- QF-PCR is limited to chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y
- Other chromosomal aneuploidies are not excluded
- Single gene mutations or small intragenic deletions/duplications are not detected by these methods

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
